approved: Crimes Amendment (Repeal Mandatory Minimum Sentences) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would remove mandatory minimum sentences from Commonwealth law.
It would repeal the sentencing provisions added by the Criminal Code Amendment (Hate Crimes) Act 2025.
The explanatory memorandum does not specify when the repeal would start or whether it applies to existing sentences.
Remove the sentencing rules enacted in the Criminal Code Amendment (Hate Crimes) Act 2025.
End the requirement for courts to impose a minimum term for certain offences.
People convicted under the hate crimes law, particularly First Nations and other marginalised groups, and the courts that would no longer have to impose fixed minimum sentences.

Moved to suspend standing orders and restore the Australian Education Legislation Amendment (Prohibiting the Indoctrination of Children) Bill 2020 and twelve other listed bills to the Notice Paper for consideration at the second reading stage; both questions were agreed to.
